direction.premise: A physical abandoned maze that literally rearranges forgotten parts. Player feels alone until the corridor breathes behind them.
direction.composition: The 3D world fills the screen; one faint axial compass and a tiny slab of health float on top. Menu type wraps around a ghostly lens aperture rather than a card.
direction.shapeLanguage: Brutalist tiled service tunnels, sharp double-door apertures, bare concrete ribs, faceless rectangular sentries.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Tarnished calcium walls, streaked aged concrete, matt graphite ceilings, amber mnemonic relics, fog and hard light.
direction.paletteLogic: Deep petrol shadow and muted pale lime grey architecture. Amber appears only where objective or life is recoverable; bruised carmine on threats.
direction.typography: Tall compressed mechanical sans for status; huge tightly stacked uppercase title; no atmospheric microcopy during play.
direction.signature: The unchangeable four-way structural spine of every chunk is surrounded by peripheral rooms that morph only after the player leaves; a faint rotating target pointer remains stable as architecture shifts.
direction.distinction: Unlike GLOAMSTEP's overhead pixel board and MELT//CRYPT's ornamental combat arena, this is first-person embodied navigation through volumetric concrete with deliberately minimal controls.
direction.spatialRationale: Every pixel beyond occasional floating controls belongs to rendered corridors; joystick/looking surfaces use separate thumb zones with no document scrolling.

comparisons.spatialDifference: First-person WebGL field with spatial walls and fog replaces a framed top-down tile arena.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Continuous physical walking and looking replace swipe-by-tile turns.

comparisons.spatialDifference: No action-toolbar or heavily composed weapon frame; nearly screen-filling desolate geometric hallways.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Exposure, retreat and collecting anchors rather than projectiles and execution.

production.renderer: Pure authored WebGL geometry and custom light/fog shader, zero runtime CDN dependencies; generated chunks with cached vertex buffers.
production.focalAsset: Stable two-cell architectural passages, procedurally carved rooms and original faceless phantom meshes.

motion.character: Inertial head bob tied only to actual movement, no idle screen wobble.
motion.action: Thumb drag or mouse looks and WASD walks through real geometric rooms.
motion.anticipation: A low crimson hue and a distant elongated silhouette warn of a nearby genuine pursuer.
motion.response: Torch direction immediately reveals detail and can dispel fake phantoms; pressing sprint changes physical movement speed.
motion.followThrough: Collected amber mnemonic fades, counter increments and compass redirects to the next source.
motion.interruption: Pointer cancellation clears sticks; tab suspension pauses simulation and autosaves.
motion.reducedMotion: User motion reduction disables head-bob and incidental shake while preserving traversal.

evidence.expectedChange: Main menu disappears and the first-person 3D labyrinth becomes controllable with compass and health displayed.

architecture.primaryVerb: Move through geometric 3D corridors and collect memory sources while evading pursuers.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Position changes with WASD/thumb; corridor parallax and torch cone move continuously; collectible disappears when reached.
architecture.spatialRationale: Full phone width remains 3D scene. Peripheral overlays do not reduce field of view; buttons sit inside thumb reach only.

comparisons.spatialDifference: A continuous 3D maze seen through eye-height perspective replaces a flat single-screen competitive gravity or pulling arena.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Player explores branching hallways and survives fleeting pursuers through spatial awareness, instead of issuing short symmetric competitive pushes.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Eye-level corridor depth and fullscreen personal horror replace the tiny cooperative warehouse seen as a planar two-avatar puzzle.
comparisons.interactionDifference: One person navigates and turns their viewpoint with continuous independent controls rather than splitting axes between two human players.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Rendered brutalist tunnels and open 3D fog replace the paper manuscript and framed shared writing workspace.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Survival movement and exploration have immediate spatial consequences rather than alternating between text drafting and chapter reveal.

comparisons.spatialDifference: An eye-height full-bleed 3D labyrinth, without Zamazka's tabletop image restorations and picture comparison gallery.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Continuous dual-stick physical exploration and real-time survival replaces restoring and voting on altered artworks.

comparisons.spatialDifference: A narrow first-person concrete labyrinth with nearly invisible interface replaces the readable broad overhead village model.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Every swipe turns the character's eyes while movement can provoke stalkers, rather than selecting or observing historical households.

comparisons.spatialDifference: The player sees a foggy 3D service tunnel, not Folio's bright framed illustration and brush workbench.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Walk, turn and hide from silhouettes instead of drawing strokes, filling regions and managing layers.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Full-bleed first-person 3D environment replaces a flat framed dungeon viewport.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Continuous twin-stick navigation replaces discrete map steps.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Deep volumetric corridors replace overhead time-echo puzzle grid.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Moving and surviving while forgetting spaces replaces placing route echoes.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Eye-height corridor navigation replaces top-down abbey and bottom bell plate.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Free movement with 3D flashlight replaces pivoting a fixed lamp.
